On the interval \([-6,-1)\), the graph is a continuous straight line, and on \((-1,6]\), it is a continuous curve. The only break occurs at \(x=-1\):

- From the left, the graph approaches \(3\) (open circle at \((-1,3)\)).
- From the right and at the point itself, the graph is at \(-3\) (solid dot at \((-1,-3)\)).

Since these values do not match, the function has a jump discontinuity at \(x=-1\). No other point in \([-6,6]\) has such a break.

\[
\boxed{x=-1}
\]
